initial: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: actual production-style 2D game VFX sprite sheet with a genuinely transparent alpha background, NOT a diagram or concept painting. Create an original broad outward-sweeping melee crescent wave for the Warden in a dark fantasy isometric arena game. Four sequential animation frames arranged in a strict 2 by 2 grid, all equal square cells, consistent scale, identical stationary attack-origin anchor at the center of each cell, generous transparent padding. Read frames left to right then top to bottom. The wave faces right and opens back toward the origin: a broad continuous 110-degree curved arc with its convex leading edge on the right and two smoothly tapered tips on the upper-right and lower-right. It is one clean crescent energy blade: crisp luminous warm ivory leading edge, restrained pale gold thin inner body, soft short transparent trailing fade, hollow transparent center. Polished smooth raster game asset with precise antialiased edges and controlled shading, no sketching. The arc lies flat on the ground with true 2:1 isometric compression: horizontal radius is twice vertical radius. Four stages: 1 small crescent emerging close to the origin; 2 crescent expands to roughly 65 percent reach; 3 full crescent at maximum radius with sharp brightest edge, outer horizontal radius about 40 percent of cell width; 4 same full radius fading to transparent with intact readable shape. Keep the leading rim thickness nearly constant as radius expands, NOT a tiny sprite blown up with a thick blurry edge. Full 110-degree forward sweep, not a full circle, not a narrow projectile. Keep the sprite efficient and restrained, usable at small TV-game sizes. Absolutely no character, sword, enemy, scenery, floor, HUD, text, numbers, labels, arrows, borders, grid lines, checkerboard, solid background, hand-drawn construction lines, fire, lightning, starburst, runes, sparks or separate decoration. Alpha outside the four crescent effects must be fully transparent. This deliverable is the sprite sheet itself, not a picture of a sprite sheet.
